salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when people need to walk into a room, connect a laptop or room source, and get content onto the display without cable swapping or technical confusion.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It improves the day-to-day room experience by bringing source switching, display connection and often USB collaboration into one predictable room core.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Meeting rooms, classrooms, training spaces and collaboration rooms where users need simple presentation from modern laptops.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Talk about the user journey: connect, present, share, hand off to the display or wider system.
talkTrack: It focuses on getting presentation sources to the room display cleanly.
It is strongest when the customer wants a reliable wired room experience.
Use it where the display path stays local or is handled by another transport product.
discoveryPrompts: How many laptops or room sources need to connect?
Do users need USB devices such as a camera, speakerphone or touch display?
Are there one, two or more displays in the room?
Does the room need a feed for recording, Teams, Zoom, or AV-over-IP?
positioningNotes: Lead with user simplicity and room workflow.
Use the port count and USB class as proof after the application is understood.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not sell it as a generic matrix unless the customer only cares about source-to-display routing.

systemIntegrator.headline: SW-0401-H2: deployment and commissioning view
systemIntegrator.pitch: Use this view when the installer needs to understand where the room core sits, which user connections land at the table or wall, and what leaves the room toward displays, USB devices or downstream systems.
systemIntegrator.value: Turns the sales conversation into practical install checks: location, cabling, signal direction, dependencies, control and commissioning risk.
talkTrack: Check the practical signal path around HDMI before finalising the design.

consultant.label: Consultant / technical
consultant.headline: SW-0401-H2: architecture fit and trade-off view
consultant.pitch: Use this view to decide whether the product is the right room-core architecture or whether the room should move toward a simpler switcher, matrix, extender or AV-over-IP design.
consultant.value: Helps separate a technically possible product choice from the strongest design choice for the application, budget, risk and future expansion.
talkTrack: Validate the application first, then decide whether this product family is the cleanest architecture.
Compare against simpler or more scalable alternatives where the requirement is fixed, expandable, distance-led or conferencing-led.
Use the specification as evidence after the room workflow and signal architecture are clear.
discoveryPrompts: Is this requirement driven by user experience, source/display routing, distance, USB, collaboration, network distribution, processing or control?

positioningNotes: Use for architectural judgement, product-family selection and proposal-safe trade-off language.
